_comment: How wide a line may be before the engine wraps it, per window.
The engine checks the limit at $C1:9232, BEFORE it draws the glyph:
lda $0E2C / and #$00FF / cmp $00 / bcc $924A   -- $00 = the new column
$0E2A counts two units per character cell, and our adapter keeps it in
the same unit ($0E2A = PEN / 4), so the check bounds our pixels too.
Going over does not crash -- it wraps early and DROPS the glyph that
crossed the line, which reads as a character quietly going missing.
$0E2C bit $1000 indents every line after the first by one cell, which is
why `indent` costs eight pixels on continuation lines.
